data.description:
## Problem

Before the 25-minute main-thread stall that spawned C11-209, the hang log recorded seven shorter episodes of 2.4 s to 10.7 s with the same cause/fingerprint, spread over the preceding stretch. Each was below or near the Sentry threshold, each was written to the local log, and none of them reached the operator or the events stream. The wedge was predictable from data c11 already had; c11 just never said anything.

`MainThreadHangMonitor` (Sources/MainThreadHangMonitor.swift) already classifies each episode into a `MainThreadHangSignature` with a `fingerprint` array and a `cause` label, and `handleHang` / `handleRecovery` run per episode on the watchdog thread. There is no cross-episode memory.

Found by the C11-209 delegator.

## Fix

Add a small cross-episode tracker on the watchdog thread:

- Keep a rolling record of completed episodes (fingerprint key, cause, duration, end uptime) bounded in size and time (suggest: last 10 minutes, at most 64 entries).
- When N episodes (suggest N=3) with the same fingerprint key complete within the window, and the cause is one `isWorthReporting` would accept (never `runloop-idle`), emit a precursor signal exactly once per fingerprint per window (re-arm after the window slides past).
- The signal must land in all three places: (1) a `=== c11 hang.precursor ... ===` block in hang.log carrying the fingerprint, count, window and durations; (2) the c11 file-first events stream (the `c11 events tail` stream; read `~/.claude/skills/c11/references/events.md` for the envelope and v1 taxonomy, and add a `hang.precursor` event with a payload that names cause, culprit, count, window_ms and the durations); (3) one Sentry event through the existing `SentryEventBudgetGate` path, tagged `hang.precursor=true` with the same fingerprint so it groups with the eventual wedge.
- Off-main only. No modal, no alert, no `runModal`, no UI mutation from the watchdog thread. If you want a visible operator hint, do it via the existing notification store on `DispatchQueue.main.async` and keep it a single non-blocking notification per window; that part is optional.
- Cost: constant time per episode; no allocation in the suspend window.

## Tests

Pure-logic tests in `c11LogicTests` against a `HangPrecursorTracker` (or similar) struct with injectable clock: fewer than N in window does not fire; N fires once; the same fingerprint does not fire again until the window has slid; a different fingerprint fires independently; `runloop-idle` never fires; old entries age out. No source-text assertions.

## Validation

CI is the gate. Do NOT run `xcodebuild` locally on this machine (one build per machine rule). Push, open the PR, watch `gh pr checks`, iterate until green. If a local runtime demonstration is feasible without a build, describe it; otherwise say plainly that validation is tests plus CI.
data.title: Hang monitor: repeated same-fingerprint episodes never surface as a precursor warning

data.body:
Plan (delegator, branch c11-221-hang-precursor):

1. New pure-logic `Sources/HangPrecursorTracker.swift`: bounded ring of completed episodes (fingerprint, cause, culprit, durationMs, endUptime). N=3, window=600s (10 min), maxEntries=64. `record(fingerprint:cause:culprit:durationMs:nowUptime:) -> Precursor?` prunes by window + cap, filters out causes `MainThreadHangMonitor.isWorthReporting` rejects (so runloop-idle never records or fires), counts same-fingerprint entries in window, and fires at most once per fingerprint per window (re-arm once now - firedAt >= window). Injectable clock via the nowUptime parameter; no threads, no wall clock.

2. `MainThreadHangMonitor`: remember the episode's first-capture descriptor on the watchdog thread; on `handleRecovery` feed the tracker and, on a Precursor, fan out to the three sinks:
   - hang.log: a `=== c11 hang.precursor ... ===` block via the existing `appendToLog` (additive; not restructuring it, C11-220 owns that function).
   - events stream: new `hang.precursor` taxonomy member on `EventEnvelope.EventType` + `EventEmitter.emitHangPrecursor`, payload {cause, culprit, count, window_ms, durations_ms, fingerprint}. No subject refs (process-level, like conversation.resume.mode). Schema + skills/c11/references/events.md updated.
   - Sentry: one `sentryCaptureWarning` with `category: sentryHangCategory` (so the existing beforeSend SentryEventBudgetGate charges it to the hang budget exactly once) tagged `hang.precursor=true`, fingerprinted with the episode's own fingerprint so it groups with the eventual wedge.

3. Off-main only, watchdog thread. No UI mutation, no alert/runModal. Skipping the optional operator notification: TerminalNotificationStore.addNotification requires a tabId and a process-level watchdog signal has no natural owning tab, so that is a separate product call.

4. Tests in c11LogicTests (`c11Tests/HangPrecursorTrackerTests.swift`, wired into the c11LogicTests target by hand since the project has no PBXFileSystemSynchronizedRootGroup): under N no fire; N fires once with the right count/durations; no re-fire until the window slides; independent fingerprints; runloop-idle never; entries age out; ring cap evicts oldest. Behavioral only, no source-text assertions.

5. No local xcodebuild. CI is the gate.

Done. PR: https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/c11/pull/436 (branch c11-221-hang-precursor, head cf51ff7ad, rebased onto 925154f58 after C11-220 merged). NOT merged; orchestrator owns that.

CI: all green on the rebased head, including compat-tests (macos-15) at 9m and the `build` job that runs the logic-test gate. drawbridge-merge shows 'skipping' as usual.

What landed:
- `Sources/HangPrecursorTracker.swift` (new): pure value type, injected clock. Bounded time-windowed ring of completed episodes. N=3, window=600s, maxEntries=64. Fires at most once per fingerprint per window, re-arming only once the window has slid past the warning. Causes `MainThreadHangMonitor.isWorthReporting` rejects (today only runloop-idle) are neither counted nor retained, so they cannot crowd a real run out of the ring. Constant work per episode, no allocation near the suspend window.
- `MainThreadHangMonitor`: remembers the episode's classification from its FIRST capture (a recapture can land in a different frame of the same wedge; a run keyed on a moving classification would never accumulate), feeds the tracker in handleRecovery, and fans a Precursor out to the three sinks. Watchdog thread only, no UI mutation, no alert, no runModal, no dlog.

Three sinks:
1. hang.log — `=== c11 hang.precursor <ts> pid=<pid> cause=<c> count=3 windowMs=600000 spanMs=<n> durationsMs=[2410,6180,10740] fingerprint=main-thread-hang/xpc-sync-wait culprit=<mangled> ===` via the existing `appendToLog(_:)` with C11-220's episodeBoundary defaulting to false. It is written after the hang.end boundary record, so a rotation triggered by hang.end happens first and the precursor lands in the fresh log rather than orphaned at the tail of a rolled file.
2. Events stream — new `hang.precursor` v1 taxonomy member + `EventEmitter.emitHangPrecursor`. No subject refs (process-level, like conversation.resume.mode). Payload: {cause, culprit, count, window_ms, span_ms, durations_ms, fingerprint}. Schema, a valid fixture, and skills/c11/references/events.md all updated.
3. Sentry — one `sentryCaptureWarning` tagged hang.precursor=true (plus hang.cause, hang.precursor_count, hang.culprit), fingerprinted with the episode's own fingerprint so it groups with the eventual wedge, categorised `hang` so the existing beforeSend SentryEventBudgetGate charges it exactly once. Deliberately did NOT call the gate at the producing side; that would spend two slots on one event.

Drive-by fix: `spec/event-envelope.v1.schema.json` was missing the four flag.* types, emitted since C11-163 but never added to the enum, so tests_v2/test_events_parity.py failed its live-parity layer against any real instance log on main. Added them alongside hang.precursor; the test now passes over 1,709 live lines locally.

Tests: c11Tests/HangPrecursorTrackerTests.swift, member of the c11LogicTests target, 13 behavioural cases (under N no fire; N fires once with exact count/durations/span/culprit; the C11-209 sub-threshold shape still warns; no re-fire inside the window; fires again once it slides; independent fingerprints; runloop-idle never and not retained; excluded cause does not feed another run; empty fingerprint ignored; spread wider than the window never accumulates; entries age out; aged-out entries cannot complete a later run; ring cap evicts oldest). Injected uptimes, no threads, no source-text assertions.

Both new files wired into project.pbxproj by hand with fresh unique IDs (no PBXFileSystemSynchronizedRootGroup in this project); plutil -lint passes. The rebase conflicted only in pbxproj, in four hunks where C11-220's HangLogRotatorTests entries sat adjacent to mine; resolved keeping both sides. MainThreadHangMonitor.swift auto-merged cleanly.

Deliberately NOT done:
- The optional operator notification. TerminalNotificationStore.addNotification requires a tabId and a process-level watchdog signal has no natural owning tab; picking one arbitrarily would be wrong and adding operator-visible noise is a product call worth its own ticket. The events stream already gives a watching agent the signal.
- No local xcodebuild, per the one-build-per-machine rule. Local checks were swiftc -frontend -parse, plutil -lint, and the full events parity test including its live-instance layer; CI was the build/test gate.
- Did not run scripts/sync-installed-skills.sh: this PR edits skills/c11/references/events.md, and syncing from an unmerged worktree would install un-merged skill content on the operator's machine. Flagged in the PR body for the maintainer to run after merge.

PASS. PR #436 squash-merged after rebase onto C11-220; CI fully green including the logic-test gate (13 HangPrecursorTrackerTests) and events parity. Orchestrator reviewed: bounded time-windowed ring (N=3, 10 min, 64 entries) keyed on the first capture's fingerprint, fires once per fingerprint per window, runloop-idle excluded; sinks are hang.log block after the hang.end boundary, hang.precursor v1 event with schema and fixture, and one Sentry warning sharing the wedge fingerprint through the existing budget gate. Optional operator notification deliberately skipped (no owning tab). Drive-by: flag.* types added to the v1 envelope schema, which parity tests had been failing on.
